name: Divided Realms DR-dev-0.1b: The Fishing Update (bring your own 1.130 client)
body:
# Divided Realms DR-dev-0.1b: The Fishing Update

**Join us on Discord: https://discord.gg/pq73ErExR**

The Fishing Update with the fixes from your first Discord reports. It replaces DR-dev-0.1a, for the **original retail
1.130 client**. Grab a pole: you can fish now. Fish with your friends, and take them all the way to Atlantis.

**This download contains no game client.** You use your own Dark Age of Camelot install.

## Fixed in 0.1b
- **Walled-in border keep gates:** at Castle Sauvage, Snowdonia Fortress, Svasud Faste, Vindsaul Faste and Druim Cain
  the gate opened but you couldn't walk out ("Invalid ZonePoint ... ID 191/193"). Live's client points those gates at
  New Frontiers; the client patch now takes those jumps out. The launcher patches your client copy again on its first
  start.
- **Empty battleground portal keeps:** Abermenai's portal keeps had no guards or NPCs and Murdaigean's only Siege
  Masters. Both now have the guards, Hastener, merchants and Siegemasters Thidranki has.
- **No realm points or experience in a bot group:** if you grouped with gamebots, you got nothing for the enemy bots
  your group mates killed. Their kills now count toward your group's share, as they already did for monsters.
- **Kill messages for bots:** an enemy or friendly gamebot dying in RvR now shows the "was just killed by" line, like a
  player.
- **Bots back from the capital:** a gamebot that released in a battleground came back from its capital; it now comes
  back at its own portal keep.
- **Rez for Heretics and Valkyries:** a dead gamebot next to a Heretic or Valkyrie released after 20 seconds instead of
  waiting for the rez. It now waits, as it does for a Cleric.
- **Companions level with you** (up to 50) on their next idle turn, with stats, specs, spells and gear for that level.
  /raid and the companion raid open at level 50 or higher, not only at exactly 50.
- **Launcher:** says which serverconfig.xml value stops the server, and why START SERVER does nothing when another
  server already uses the port.

**Already playing DR-dev-0.1a or 0.1?** Extract this over your folder and replace every file. Your world and characters
stay; the launcher adds the new portal keep guards to your world on its next start.

## Gone fishing

Fishing is a trade skill of its own, from 1 to 1000.

- **Cast a line:** face open water with a fishing pole and type `/fish`. You sit down, a bobber floats where your line
  lands, and you keep casting until you move or type `/fish stop`. `/fish active` lets you reel in each bite yourself.
  No pole yet? `/fish pole` gives you one. Poles have their **own long fishing-rod model**, held out in front of you;
  the launcher adds it to your client copy.
- **Every realm has its own waters:** brown trout and pike in Albion, arctic char and halibut in Midgard, salmon and
  bream in Hibernia, in four sizes. Then there's the odd old boot, a waterlogged chest full of coin (one in four also
  holds a magic item), and a few **legendary fish**. Legendaries are rare enough that the whole server hears about it
  when one is landed.
- **Craft better poles:** `/fish craft` makes the Oaken, Ironwood, Heartwood and Runewood Angler's poles from wood,
  thread, cloth and leather sold by crafting merchants in every realm. A better pole lands better fish and gets bites
  sooner. Each pole only teaches up to a point (250, 500, 750, 1000), so keep crafting to keep improving.
- **Make camp:** Campfire, Bedroll and Tent Camp Kits put a camp down for 15, 20 or 30 minutes. You and your group
  (companion bots too) get health, power and endurance back near it, twice as fast sitting down, and fishing beside a
  bigger camp lands better fish.
- **Cook your catch:** `/fish cook` by a burning campfire turns raw fish into Grilled Fish, Smoked Fish or an Angler's
  Feast, for 20 minutes of faster regeneration.
- **Fish are worth money:** a small fish sells for a couple of silver and a trophy for about 2 gold. Fish stack in
  your bags.
- **Find a spot:** `/fish spots` lists shores in each realm and `/fish go <number>` takes you to one in your own realm.
  `/fish mark` saves your own spots.
- Monsters leave you alone while you hold the pole and aren't fighting. `/fish stats` shows your skill and pole.

## Fish with your friends

- **Host for Friends** is one button and a password. It gives you an **invite code**: send it with the password, and
  friends paste it into **Join Friend**. Nobody types addresses.
- **Bring your own character** to a friend's world. Choose it in Join Friend and it travels with its gear and coin.
  It's locked at home while it visits, and **COME HOME** brings it back with everything it earned. This has been played
  between two PCs over the internet, both ways.
- **Bots join in.** Say you're LFG and a bot near your level sends you a tell and an invitation. `/bots hunt`,
  `/bots attack`, `/bots follow` and `/bots status` direct the bots in your group. On 1.130, bots show as player
  characters, with player name plates and movement.
- **Guild bots:** gamebots you invite into your guild earn it merit as they level and pay your dues into the guild
  bank from what they loot.
- Camp kits, cooked food and group regeneration work for the whole party.

## Fish in Atlantis

Trials of Atlantis is open and alive.

- **All of Atlantis is populated:** about 36,000 monsters and NPCs across every Atlantis zone and all three realms.
  Monsters roam and chase on new navigation meshes, merchants carry their full stock, and Djinn stones take you
  between zones.
- **Boats work:** every dock sells tickets, and the return boats go to Oceanus Hesperos. A boat bought from a
  shipwright deploys with `/boat summon` (or use it from your bags while swimming); steer it by setting a ground target.
  You can swim and dive, and lava burns.
- **Artifacts are back,** with stats and abilities rebuilt, signature effects included, such as Shades of Mist's shade
  form and the Traitor's Dagger's vampiric mist.
  - Defeat an artifact's encounter with your group and every member gets credit, for a **level 10 artifact**.
  - Atlantean Glass drops from Atlantis monsters, and buys credit from Aphaestia for a **level 0 artifact**.
  - Artifacts level up from any experience you earn, realm points included.
  - Scholars swap versions of an artifact and keep its level.
  - Artifact keys drop: loot tables now roll as written.
- **Master Levels:** all 95 trial steps of Master Levels 1 to 10.
- Level 45 and higher gamebots hunt Atlantis too, riding the boats and using the Djinn.

## Also in this update

**Bots**
- Gamebots do classic quests while they level and craft at real forges, and you can pay a bot crafter to make you an
  upgrade.
- Bots hunt Darkness Falls: PvE from level 20, PvP from level 45, solo and in groups.
- Bot armor works like a player's, archer bots fire the real archery shots, and tank bots Protect, Guard and Intercept
  for their group.
- Bots try harder fights (orange, red, purple) and learn which monsters beat them.
- Every real player in a dragon raid gets at least one item.

**Combat and classes**
- Floating combat numbers, fight reports and buff and pet windows, drawn by the launcher's overlay.
- Every class was checked against live 1.130a: spec points, hit points, gear, race pairs and a round of spell and
  style fixes.
- Archery spell shots (Long Shot, Power Shot and others) no longer miss every target above yellow con.
- Spell damage-over-time ticks no longer scale with stats. Bonedancer and Storm Sovereign fixes, and the Healer's Eir
  and Bard's Ivy buffs work.
- **Power regeneration is 1.5 times the classic rate and no longer halves below 50% power,** for players and bots
  alike. You can change both in the launcher's Living Server tab.
- Power, endurance or health that stopped regenerating until you relogged now restarts by itself.

**World**
- Fixed: the invisible walls at the Castle Sauvage, Snowdonia Fortress and Druim Cain gates, the Darkness Falls exits
  in Legion's hall, keep door headings and border keep doors.
- Relics survive a carrier's trip through a portal.
- Dead players can't loot, and creatures with a sliver of health left no longer fall early.

**Launcher and server**
- A redesigned launcher with a Bots page.
- Bot Watch, a live browser map of the bots and groups in each region, opens while your server runs.
- **Safer saves:** the world database writes safely even if the server crashes, checks itself at every start and keeps
  a daily backup in `runtime\data\backups` (the last 7). Seven backups take about 2 GB of disk; the server setting
  `db_backup_keep` changes how many.
- **Import progress:** installed in a new folder? Options > Update and repair > **IMPORT PROGRESS** brings your
  account, characters, items, bots, houses, guilds, fishing and artifacts from your old folder.
- **Repair client:** Options > Update and repair > **REPAIR CLIENT** checks every file of the game's client copy against
  your Dark Age of Camelot folder, restores anything damaged or missing and patches Divided Realms in again. Your game
  settings and character layouts are kept.
- The original client files that came from the game are no longer kept in the repository.

**GitHub issues fixed:** #1 and #7 (bots standing while dead), #2 and #6 (invisible walls), #3 (Darkness Falls steps),
#4 (archery always missing).

Thanks to the forks we took fixes from this round: chris4aker's Living Server (save safety, guild bots and power
regeneration), Nikse77, lometur's HearthDAoC, shadowofze's True165, Rmarcoux86 (the fishing this update grew from) and
OpenDAoC.

## Checked for this build
- **0.1b:** all 5,707 server tests, 262 launcher tests and the client patch tool tests pass. On a private copy of the
  test server, a level 17 Heretic killed gamebots in Abermenai (realm points and experience paid), a level 22 Heretic
  grouped with a gamebot was paid for the bot's kills without doing damage of their own, and a dead grouped bot waited
  for the Heretic's Revive and took it. The world update was applied to the DR-dev-0.1a, DR-dev-0.1 and 0.38-dev10
  worlds and gave this release's world each time. This zip's own server started from a clean copy with no errors, made
  a new account on first login, and has the Abermenai portal keep guards. The gate zone jump fix was checked against
  the client's data only, not walked through in a client.
- **0.1a:** 262 launcher tests and the rez tests pass. The setup was checked on your stock `gamedata.mpk`, on a
  later-live one and on Eden's real one. From this zip, the launcher set up a client whose `gamedata.mpk` is another
  build and prepared the world. The game server of this zip was not started; the world is unchanged from DR-dev-0.1.
  The DR-dev-0.1 checks below still apply:
- **Automated tests:** all 5,692 server tests, 257 launcher tests and the package and client patch tool tests pass,
  including the whole client patch built from a pristine 1.130 client and applied by the launcher's own code.
- **Import progress:** a real test world (143 characters, 3,000 bots, 106,723 items, fishing and artifacts) imported
  into this release's world by the same engine, with nothing lost. The two new launcher buttons themselves haven't been
  clicked in the window yet.
- **Playing with friends:** a friend brought a character over the internet to a hosted world and took it home again,
  more than once.
- **Atlantis and artifacts:** the first Atlantis play found standing monsters, thin merchants and broken boats, and
  all three were fixed. Artifact credit, Glass, levelling, version swaps and the signature abilities were run on a test
  server with the test client.
- **On a private server copy:** this build ran 15 minutes with about 3,000 bots: no errors, a clean stop, and the new
  database checks and backup.
- **Not played by a person yet:** fishing beyond the first tries, cooking and camp kits; guild merit and dues; most of
  the Master Level trials (one fight played); the Darkness Falls bot goals.

## Requirements
- Dark Age of Camelot at the **1.130** client version. The setup accepts only that build's `game.dll` (SHA256 `3915a495…`).
- **Played on Eden?** The Eden client changes game files in your Dark Age of Camelot folder (loading screens, maps, zone
  borders, emotes and catalogs), and the live patcher doesn't put the originals back. The setup can't use a folder
  Eden changed and says so. Install Dark Age of Camelot again into a new folder (or use another unchanged copy) and
  choose that one. Divided Realms itself uses nothing from Eden.
- The Windows feature **.NET Framework 3.5**, for the client's connector. The game's own .NET runtime is included.
- About 8 GB free disk, plus room for the daily world backups.
- To play together, everyone needs this same build.

## How to play
1. Extract the zip and double-click **START DIVIDED REALMS.cmd**.
2. The launcher asks for your DAoC folder. It copies your client into the game folder and patches the copy. **Your own
   install is not changed.**
3. **START SERVER**, then **ENTER REALM**. Your account is created on the first login.

## Updating

**From DR-dev-0.1a or DR-dev-0.1:** close the launcher, extract this download over your folder and replace every
file. Your world and characters are kept; on its next start the launcher adds this release's world fixes (after a backup)
and patches your client copy again.

**Same folder (easiest), from 0.38-dev8 or a 0.38-dev10 a friend gave you:** close the launcher, extract this download
over your folder and replace every file. Your world and characters are kept. On its next start the launcher brings your
world up to date and patches your client copy again (it may ask for your Dark Age of Camelot folder once). The first
start also moves power regeneration to the new rate, unless you had changed it yourself.

**New folder:** extract this download somewhere new, start its launcher once and set up the client, then in
**Options > Update and repair** press **IMPORT PROGRESS** and choose your old folder. Your account, characters, items,
bots, houses, guilds, fishing and artifacts come across, and your login is the old one. The old folder is only read, and
the new folder's world is backed up first. Stop the server before importing.

**Something wrong with the game client** (crashes, missing art, a file changed by another program)? **REPAIR CLIENT**
in the same place puts it right without touching your settings.

## Known limits
- The client has no fishing animation: you sit with the rod held out. The trade skill window doesn't show a Fishing line
  yet; `/fish stats` shows your skill.
- Some Atlantis merchants still have thin stock. Bots can't reach the Ashen Isles. Boss balance for a real group hasn't
  been tuned.
- Hosting over the internet doesn't work for a host whose provider shares addresses (CGNAT); the window tells you.
- The fishing rod uses catalog numbers 4927 and 4928. A `gamedata.mpk` that already uses them (Eden's does) keeps its
  own objects there, so the pole looks like that object.
- Everything listed under Known limits in 0.38-dev8 still applies.

## Download check
`DividedRealms-DR-dev-0.1b-Fishing-Update.zip` · SHA256 `1ad8e3bfeac005ea0d34222b7515441888cdba3168d2e995f0cf55d263428e1c`
(1,200,457,112 bytes)

**Questions, bugs, fish stories: https://discord.gg/pq73ErExR**

name: Divided Realms 0.38-dev8 modern test (bring your own 1.130 client)
body:
The eighth development test build for the **original retail 1.130 client**. It fixes the battlegrounds and RvR dungeons on a stock client, and it carries a round of bot route, keep and raid fixes from long test runs.

**This download contains no game client.** You use your own Dark Age of Camelot install.

### What's new since 0.38-dev7

**Battlegrounds and RvR dungeons on your own client:**
- The four battlegrounds, Dodens Gruva, Summoner's Hall and Marfach Caverns now load on a stock 1.130 client. Before, going there dropped you to character select or out of bounds.
- The launcher adds these regions to its copy of your client and builds Abermenai's terrain from your client's own Thidranki files. Marfach's map isn't in 1.130, so the client patch carries it. An existing client copy is patched on the next start.

**Bot travel:**
- Albion bots bound for Pennine Mountains no longer turn back and forth at the Black Mountains North border. In one test run that loop cost 574 bots 2,399 goals.
- Bots stop heading for a zone crossing they can't reach. Once three bots give up beside one, the others use a different crossing for two hours. The crossings behind a wall in Valley of Bri Leith caused 408 give-ups in one run.
- A bot inside its own realm's keep can leave through the doors. After a capture, armies used to be stuck inside until they were teleported home.
- Bots back away from monsters they can't fight on hills as well as flat ground. In test runs, retreats that found no way out fell from 23% to 5%.
- Fixed a server error when two kills in the same moment levelled up the same bot.

**Hall of the Corrupt:**
- 31 monsters that stood outside the 1.130 dungeon are now placed in its rooms, so a raid can reach them. Before, a raid there could end "Route blocked" with encounters left.

### Checked for this build
- **Automated tests:** all 4,890 server tests, 191 launcher tests (1 skipped) and the world-update and client-patch tool tests (1 skipped) pass.
- **In game:** the battlegrounds, on the owner's local package built with the same client patch. The Pennine fix, the retreat fix and the level-up fix each held through a 9-hour bot test run.
- **Not yet played:** the crossing rule, the keep doors and the Hall of the Corrupt raid (these passed tests, and the routes were checked on the game's navigation data, but they haven't run in a live server). Marfach Caverns hasn't been tried. Updating a dev7 folder by extracting this build over it is checked by tests only.

### Requirements
- Dark Age of Camelot at the **1.130** client version. The setup accepts only that build's `game.dll` (SHA256 `3915a495…`).
- The Windows feature **.NET Framework 3.5**, for the client's connector. The game's own .NET runtime is included.
- About 7 GB free disk.
- To play together, everyone needs this same build.

### How to play
1. Extract the zip and double-click **START DIVIDED REALMS.cmd**.
2. The launcher asks for your DAoC folder. It copies your client into the game folder and patches the copy. **Your own install is not changed.**
3. **START SERVER**, then **ENTER REALM**. Your account is created on the first login.

**Updating from 0.38-dev7 or earlier:** close the launcher, extract this download over your folder and replace every file. Your world and characters are kept.

Joining a friend and hosting work as in 0.38-dev5 (`docs/PLAY-WITH-FRIENDS.md` in the download).

### Known limits
- Hall of the Corrupt monsters were placed from the navigation data, not by eye, so some may stand in odd spots. Lord Gildas is about 2,000 units higher than his classic spot, and Lady Darra's summoned paladins still appear at their old positions.
- Everything listed under Known limits in 0.38-dev7 still applies.

### Download check
`DividedRealms-0.38-dev8-modern-test.zip` · SHA256 `456c898b549f814beab44184688e47b5a5622d529079446cfb5b8efef073d28c`
(952,042,318 bytes)

name: World Workshop 1.0.0: world, item and data editor for Offline DAoC
body:
World Workshop is a world, item and data editor for Offline DAoC. It opens in your web browser and edits the game folder you already play from: NPCs and their walking paths, items, merchants, loot, spells, quests and server settings. Every save is backed up and can be undone.

This download contains no game files. Everything you see is read from your own installed client.

## What it does

3D world:

- See your zone with its real terrain, buildings, trees and NPC models.
- Move, add, copy and delete NPCs, objects and doors, plus zone points, bind points, teleports, jump points, keeps and areas.
- Give an NPC a walking route: click the ground to add waypoints, then choose loop, back and forth or walk once.

Items:

- Browse every server item and every item appearance in your client: weapons, armor, cloaks, helms, shields and housing decorations.
- Preview items in 3D. Armor, cloaks and helms are shown on a player character (Norse, Briton or Celt, male or female), with the item's dye, mesh variant and glow effects.
- Edit stats with readable names: bonuses, damage type, slot, realm, effect.
- Sort by level, name, price, type or realm, and filter by slot or level range.
- Find problems: appearances missing from your client, items that can't be equipped, items nothing sells or drops.
- See where each item comes from: merchants, loot drops, crafting, quests, starter gear.
- Turn client art the server doesn't use yet (hundreds of armor pieces, cloaks, weapons and housing decorations) into new server items.

Merchants:

- Build merchant lists page by page and put them on any NPC.
- Pay with coins, or with any item as currency (like the Darkness Falls seal merchants). Item currency needs a server with `GameCustomCurrencyMerchant`; see Known limits.

Also:

- Game data: search and edit NPC templates, loot tables, spells, quests, server properties and other content tables. Accounts and characters are never shown.
- Server files: edit server settings and bot JSON files, with a backup on every save.
- Custom looks: give NPCs new looks painted on any client model.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit.
- An Offline DAoC game folder you already play from (the folder with `START OFFLINE DAOC.cmd`). The modern-test package works too.
- A current Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
- About 170 MB, plus room for preview caches inside your game folder.

No Python or other installs are needed. Exact building floors use the .NET 10 runtime already in your game's `tools\dotnet` folder.

## How to use

1. Extract the zip anywhere and run `WorldWorkshop.exe`. Windows may warn that the program is unsigned; choose More info, then Run anyway.
2. The first time, choose your Offline DAoC game folder. The editor remembers it. To pick another one, run `WorldWorkshop.exe --game "D:\Offline DAoC"`.
3. The editor opens in your browser. Keep its console window open while you edit.
4. Close the game and stop the server before you click Review & save. Then start the server again to load your changes.

Backups, previews and caches go to `<game>\runtime\world-workshop-data`. Restore edits undoes an earlier save without touching your characters' progress.

The first preview of each zone takes a few minutes to convert. After that it loads from the cache.

## Known limits

- Item-currency merchants need a server build that includes `GameCustomCurrencyMerchant`. Stock Offline DAoC servers don't have it yet, so that option is greyed out.
- Hood-up cloaks aren't drawn yet.
- The previews are close to the game but aren't screenshots of it. Check important changes in game.
- The editor changes database rows only. It doesn't change navigation meshes, scripts or the game client, except Custom looks, which adds new private models and can be uninstalled.
- So far it has only been tested on the author's own installs. Please report problems.

## Downloads

- `WorldWorkshop-1.0.0.zip`: the program
- `WorldWorkshop-1.0.0.zip.sha256`: its checksum, `e34bd640cbcd7c88cb4ee8f2ad2f893726fc18f438ad53a024e9ceb794a16d46`

## Licence

GPL v3, like Offline DAoC. The source is in `source/tools/world_editor` at this release's tag. Three.js is MIT-licensed.
